name: Central Mexico / Bajío (Mexico City · Puebla · Guadalajara · Guanajuato)

language.script_notes: ALTO, 'topes', -MEX names, OXXO. Nahuatl-derived place names are dense here (Tlaxcala, Cuernavaca, Iztapalapa).

road_furniture.guardrail_type: Steel W-beam; concrete barrier on the busy toll roads radiating from Mexico City.
road_furniture.line_paint: White and yellow lines; heavy 'topes' at every town, plus painted crosswalks and speed tables in the colonial centres.
road_furniture.curb_style: Painted kerbs; cobblestone streets in historic centres.
road_furniture.km_marker_style: Octagonal or crucifix concrete poles. OXXO everywhere; dense billboard and shopfront clutter; jacaranda trees lining city avenues (purple in spring).

architecture.roof_style: Flat concrete roofs with tinacos in the cities; pitched clay-tile roofs in colonial towns and villages.
architecture.wall_construction: Rendered and painted masonry in the colonial cores; unfinished brick with rebar on the vast urban periphery; stone in the oldest buildings.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Bright ochre, terracotta, blue and pink in the colonial towns; grey block on the outskirts.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Dense colonial cities with tiled church domes, cobbled streets and painted facades (Guanajuato, Morelia, Querétaro, San Miguel de Allende); sprawling Mexico City with hillside informal housing; INFONAVIT estates.

nature.vegetation: Pine-oak forest on the ranges, maguey and blue agave rows on the plateau (Jalisco's tequila country is a strong tell), maize and nopal cactus, and jacaranda and eucalyptus in the cities.
nature.terrain: A high plateau at roughly 1,800–2,400 m, rolling and fertile in the Bajío basin, ringed and studded with big volcanoes — Popocatépetl and Iztaccíhuatl by Mexico City, Nevado de Toluca, Pico de Orizaba on the eastern rim.
nature.climate_signature: Temperate highland — cool, clear, thin light, a dry winter and a rainy summer, rarely hot, with occasional frost. Snow-capped volcanoes on the horizon.

vehicles.plate_color: State plates — CDMX, Estado de México, Jalisco (yellow over light blue), Guanajuato, Puebla, Querétaro, each with its own banner.
vehicles.plate_format: State-dependent, commonly three letters and three–four digits.
vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: Heavy city traffic, pink Mexico City taxis, VW 'combi' collective vans, the full Nissan/VW mix; VW Beetles still common in some towns.

google_coverage.coverage_notes: Very dense coverage across the Mexico City megalopolis and the Bajío.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country — colonial towns, pine-oak highlands, ALTO, OXXO, tinacos
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The centre is a temperate plateau with big volcanoes, agave fields and prosperous colonial cities; the south is rougher folded mountains, poorer roads, more visible indigenous presence and more jungle.
The centre is cool highland pine-oak with volcanoes and dense cities; the north is flat hot desert with cactus and spread-out towns.

confusion_set.shared_traits: High-altitude light, colonial architecture, agave/cactus vegetation
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Stop signs read ALTO not PARE; Mexican state plates and OXXO; Nahuatl place names rather than Quechua.
